introduction: Hetty has been thinking about you all morning, and she is going to say it to your face. She does not think she is being unkind. She thinks she is being interesting.
introductionSummary: Hetty talks to Rue the whole way round the trough — the cart, the straw, the six weeks — and never once about the water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Attacking the animal instead of the argument. How Rue arrived, how he looks, and how long he has been here tell us nothing about anything that needs deciding.

sentences.text: Rue. I have been thinking about you all morning.
You arrived in a mud cart, you know. Straw still in your ears. You don't take advice from an animal who turns up like that.

logicalFallacies.explanation: How Rue arrived is not a reason to dismiss what he says. Hetty has swapped the cart for an argument.

sentences.text: I said as much to anyone who would listen this morning. I thought you should hear it from me.

statement.summary: Hetty treats the mud cart you arrived in as a reason not to listen to you.

sentences.text: And you still look as if you slept in it. Straw in the fur, mud on the paws.
An animal who cannot keep himself tidy is hardly the animal you'd ask about anything that matters.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Straw in the fur is not evidence. Hetty is judging the speaker's appearance in place of whatever is actually at issue.

sentences.text: I don't mean it unkindly. I like you. You seem perfectly nice.

statement.summary: Hetty reads straw in the fur as a reason not to ask you about anything that matters, and means no harm by it.

sentences.text: And only six weeks! Six weeks.
You cannot know a place in six weeks. The Flock has been here generations; that is whose opinion counts.

logicalFallacies.explanation: How long Rue has lived here is not a fact about the thing under discussion. Tenure is being offered as a substitute for a reason.

sentences.text: Anyway. I thought you should hear it from me rather than from the yard.

statement.summary: Hetty treats six weeks on the farm as a reason the Flock's opinion is the one that counts.
